codeReview.summary: The implementation is clean, well-tested, and correctly satisfies all three validation assertions (VAL-RLM-001/002/003). The worker chose a ContextVar-based injection pattern that makes the tool testable without closures and consistent with the memory_tools.py stub pattern. Two non-blocking concerns exist: (1) `interpreter.start()` and `build_recursive_subquery_rlm()` calls are outside the error-catching try/except block, so startup/build failures will propagate as unhandled exceptions rather than returning a structured error dict; (2) `AgentRuntime.chat_turn()` doesn't call `set_delegate_interpreter()`, so the tool will raise RuntimeError in real production execution if the LLM selects it — but this is consistent with the memory_tools.py stub pattern and the validation contract only required the tool to be correctly implemented and testable, not fully wired end-to-end.

issues.description: interpreter.start() and build_recursive_subquery_rlm() are invoked before the try/except block (line ~90). If either throws, the exception propagates up as an unhandled exception rather than returning {status: error, error: ...}. Since the error handling wraps only the rlm() call, sandbox startup failures and RLM construction failures will cause the tool to raise instead of returning a structured error dict. The intent of the error handler seems to cover all runtime failures, not just rlm execution. Consider wrapping the entire post-interpreter-check body in the try/except.

AgentRuntime.chat_turn() does not call set_delegate_interpreter(self.interpreter) before self.agent.forward(). If the LLM selects delegate_to_rlm, it will always raise RuntimeError at runtime because _delegate_interpreter is None. The module docstring says 'Set by the agent runtime before invoking the agent' but the wiring is absent. This is consistent with the memory_tools.py stub pattern (read_core_memory/write_core_memory also raise RuntimeError when called directly), but it means the tool effectively does not work in production through AgentRuntime without additional caller-side wiring.

max_iterations=20 and max_llm_calls=50 are hardcoded constants. The feature description doesn't require configurability, but these values differ from the existing RLM configuration in _LegacyAgentRuntime (rlm_max_iterations=30, rlm_max_llm_calls=50). The lower max_iterations (20 vs 30) may be intentional for the simplified tool but is worth documenting explicitly.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The ContextVar injection pattern (ContextVar + set_X() helper that returns a Token) is used for interpreter injection in rlm_delegate.py but is not documented in AGENTS.md or the mission AGENTS.md as a canonical pattern. The worker invented it cleanly and consistently with the existing stub-tool pattern in memory_tools.py, but a future worker adding a similar tool might not know to use this pattern.

The architecture.md describes the RLM Delegation Flow as working end-to-end, but the actual wiring (who calls set_delegate_interpreter before agent.forward) is not implemented and not documented. The library/architecture.md shows this as an implemented flow, which is misleading.

summary: PASS. The rlm-delegation-tool feature is correctly implemented: delegate_to_rlm is registered via @tool_fn and discoverable by discover_tools(), the sandbox create/reuse logic works correctly, and the structured return type (dict with status/answer/error) is properly implemented and tested with 13 unit tests. All validators (pytest, lint, typecheck) passed. Two non-blocking issues are noted: (1) startup and RLM construction exceptions bypass the structured error handler and propagate as raw exceptions, and (2) AgentRuntime.chat_turn() does not inject the interpreter via set_delegate_interpreter() before running the agent, meaning the tool would fail at runtime if selected by the LLM — this is consistent with the existing stub pattern in memory_tools.py and the validation contract did not require end-to-end wiring.
